transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t keep my thoughts organized anymore, and it’s getting hard to make even simple decisions at work. My supervisor actually suggested I see someone after I made some scheduling mistakes, because I've been completely overwhelmed trying to balance my job with caring for my sick mother.
Have you been experiencing excessive worry or fear about your job, your mother's health, or other aspects of your life that seems out of proportion to the situation?

Yes, I have this intense, paralyzing worry that constantly runs through my head, especially at night when I'm trying to sleep. I keep imagining worst-case scenarios, like my mom losing her foot or a client ending up in the hospital because of my scheduling mistakes. I just feel like if anything goes wrong, it'll be completely my fault for messing up.
Can you tell me more about what triggered these feelings of overwhelm and worry, was it primarily your mother's illness or something else that started this cycle for you?

It definitely started when my mother's diabetes complications got worse. I began taking on extra shifts to cover her medical bills and driving to Mexico on my days off to help coordinate her care, which left me with no time to rest. That’s what really triggered this severe cycle of feeling completely amped up and then crashing.
Have you experienced any feelings of detachment from yourself or the world around you, as if you're observing things from outside your body or like things aren't real?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. I still feel very much connected to reality and my own body, it's just that my mind feels completely scattered and overwhelmed by everything going on.

Can you describe how your symptoms have changed or evolved since your mother's illness worsened, and have you noticed any periods where your worry and overwhelm seemed to lessen or increase in response to specific events or stressors?

These big swings between feeling wired and then crashing have actually been happening off and on for a couple of years, but they got much worse this past year when my mom's health started failing. This current low, scattered phase has been going on for about a month now. It hit me right after her doctor told us her diabetes had taken a turn for the worse.
Have you experienced any traumatic events, either recently or in the past, that might be contributing to your current state of overwhelm and worry?

No, I wouldn't say I've experienced any traumatic events like that. It's really just been the constant, heavy stress of trying to manage my work shifts and coordinating my mother's care as her health gets worse.

Can you tell me more about how long you've been experiencing these intense worries and feelings of being overwhelmed, and have they been constant since your mother's health issues began or have they waxed and waned over time?

These swings between feeling wired and crashing have actually been happening off and on for about a couple of years, but they got much worse over the past year since my mom's complications started. This current heavy, overwhelmed phase has been pretty constant for about the last month, starting right after her doctor told us her health had taken a turn for the worse.

You mentioned that your symptoms worsened significantly after your mother's health took a turn for the worse, can you describe if there was a specific moment or event related to her illness that triggered the intensification of your worry and feeling overwhelmed?

It really hit me hard about a month ago when her doctor told us her diabetes was getting much worse and she was at risk of losing her foot. Hearing that triggered this intense guilt and worry that I wasn't doing enough to care for her, and that's when this heavy, overwhelming feeling completely took over.

Can you clarify if the intense worry and feelings of being overwhelmed are primarily focused on your mother's health and your ability to care for her, or if they also encompass a broader range of topics and concerns beyond her illness?

While my mom's health is a major trigger, the overwhelm and worry go far beyond her. I'm constantly terrified of making a mistake at work that could hurt my clients, like missing their medications, and I feel like a terrible husband who is completely letting my wife down. It has gotten to the point where I feel paralyzed by basic everyday tasks, like just trying to organize and pay our bills.

Are there any specific situations, objects, or thoughts that trigger or significantly worsen your intense worry and feelings of being overwhelmed, beyond your mother's health and work-related concerns?

No, I can't really think of any other specific triggers or situations besides those. It really is just the constant pressure of my mom's failing health, the caregiving demands, and the terrifying fear of making mistakes at work that completely consume my thoughts and make me feel so overwhelmed.
Can you describe if the worry and feelings of overwhelm would lessen if your mother's health were to suddenly improve or if the caregiving responsibilities were significantly reduced?

Honestly, even if her health improved, I don't think it would completely fix things because these intense swings between feeling wired and crashing into hopelessness actually started a couple of years ago, well before her recent complications. The stress this past year has definitely made the cycles much worse, but the pattern was already there.

You've mentioned that your symptoms of intense worry and feeling overwhelmed have been present for a couple of years but worsened significantly with your mother's health decline. Can you think of any other significant life events or stressors that occurred around the time these symptoms first started, about two years ago?

I can't really recall any other specific major life events or stressors from around two years ago. I was already busy juggling my job and traveling to help some of our relatives across the border back then, but nothing else specific stands out.

Do you find that your worry and feelings of overwhelm are primarily driven by a fear of specific negative outcomes or consequences, such as your mother's health deteriorating or making mistakes at work, or are they more related to a general feeling of being unable to cope with daily life and responsibilities?

It is really a mix of both, but it's heavily driven by specific fears, like being constantly terrified my mom will lose her foot or that I'll make a mistake at work that lands a client in the hospital. Those worries then spiral into a general feeling of being completely overwhelmed and unable to handle basic daily responsibilities like paying bills or keeping my thoughts straight, which just makes me feel like I'm failing everyone.

Can you tell me if your worries are primarily about the future, such as fearing what might happen to your mother or at work, or are they also heavily focused on past events or perceived mistakes you've made?

It's really a mix of both. I'm constantly terrified about the future, fearing my mom's health will get worse and she'll lose her foot, or that I'll lose my job over my mistakes. At the same time, I'm consumed by guilt over past things, constantly beating myself up for messing up the work schedule and lying awake feeling like I've already failed my wife and my mom.
Have you been avoiding certain situations, tasks, or activities due to your intense worries or fears, such as avoiding work or social interactions?

I don't think I'm avoiding things out of fear or worry. While I do sometimes pull away from talking to people when I'm feeling really low and defeated, or struggle to get tasks like the bills done because my brain feels too scattered to organize them, it isn't because I'm trying to avoid them out of fear.
Are there any specific tasks or activities that you used to enjoy or find manageable but now find yourself consistently putting off or struggling to initiate due to your current state of mind?

I used to love working on car restoration and hosting board-game nights, but I've completely stopped doing those. Now, even basic things I used to handle easily—like filling out medication logs at work or managing our bills—have become so hard to start that my wife has had to take over the household finances because I keep dropping the ball.

Can you describe if your intense worries and feelings of being overwhelmed have been persistent and excessive, lasting for more than six months, or if they have been more episodic and directly tied to specific stressors like your mother's health issues?

They are definitely more episodic rather than one constant stretch of worry for six months. I've had these big swings between feeling wired and then crashing off and on for a couple of years now. This current heavy, drained phase has actually been going on for about a month, triggered by the news that my mom's health had taken a turn for the worse.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as persistent sadness or irritability, in addition to the intense worry and feelings of being overwhelmed that you've described?

Yes, my mood swings drastically between two extremes. Lately, I'll wake up with a heavy, empty sadness like a gray cloud on my chest and tear up for no reason, but then I'll swing to being weirdly amped up and irritable, snapping at my wife and people in traffic before crashing back down.
Can you estimate how often these mood swings from sadness to irritability occur, and are they directly tied to your worry episodes or seem to happen independently?

These swings between feeling wired and crashing into sadness have been happening off and on for a couple of years, but they've gotten much more frequent and intense since my mom's complications started. While the low periods are filled with heavy worry about my mom and work, the high, irritable phases sometimes feel like they have a mind of their own. Ultimately, the overall stress definitely seems to trigger and worsen the entire cycle.
Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt consistently better, with significantly reduced worry and improved mood, since your symptoms first started a couple of years ago?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. My mood mostly seems to swing between feeling completely drained and hopeless, or being overly wired and amped up. I don't recall having many periods of feeling truly stable or "consistently better" for that long.

Have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt consistently depressed, with little interest in activities you usually enjoy, and where these feelings seemed distinct from your usual worry and overwhelm?

Yes, I've been stuck in this deep, empty sadness for about a month now, which is definitely longer than two weeks. It feels like a heavy gray cloud is sitting on my chest, leaving me feeling completely hollow inside even when I'm with my wife or talking to my mom. These low, drained periods have actually happened off and on for a couple of years, but this current stretch has been much worse.

Can you tell me if your feelings of sadness and emptiness are present even when your worries about your mother's health and work seem to lessen or resolve, or if they are closely tied to the intensity of your worries?

Yes, that heavy, empty sadness feels constant and doesn't really go away, even when my worries temporarily quiet down. I just feel hollow inside and start tearing up for no clear reason, even during quiet moments with my wife or when talking to my mom. It's like a gray cloud is always sitting on my chest, regardless of what is going on around me.
Can you describe how your feelings of sadness and emptiness relate to your daily activities and interests, and have you noticed any changes in your ability to enjoy things you usually like to do?

This heavy, empty sadness is like a gray cloud that makes me feel completely hollow inside, even when I'm spending time with my wife or talking to my mom on the phone. Because of it, I have completely stopped participating in my usual interests, like car restoration and board-game nights. I just don't have the energy for them anymore and can't find any joy in them at all.
Can you tell me more about when you last felt interested in or enjoyed activities you previously found pleasurable, such as car restoration or board-game nights?

It’s been several months since I last did any car restoration or board-game nights. Initially, I just didn't have the time because of my busy schedule working extra shifts and caring for my mother. But lately, even if I do have a free moment, I feel too exhausted, hollow, and drained to care about or enjoy those hobbies anymore.

Can you think of any activities or hobbies that you still find some enjoyment in, even if it's just a little, or has the feeling of emptiness and sadness completely taken away any pleasure you once found in activities?

I used to love car restoration and board-game nights, but lately, with this heavy, empty sadness and constant exhaustion, I just don't have the time or energy for them. That hollow feeling has pretty much stripped away any pleasure or motivation I used to get from those activities, so there is really nothing I enjoy right now.

Can you clarify if the intense worry and feelings of being overwhelmed are the primary issues you're struggling with, or if the persistent sadness and loss of interest in activities are more prominent and troubling to you?

Honestly, both are incredibly difficult and feel connected because my mood constantly swings. I'll have periods of intense, overwhelming worry about my mom's health and messing up at work that keep my mind racing at night. But then I'll crash into this deep, defeated sadness where I feel completely hollow inside, like a heavy gray cloud is sitting on my chest.
Can you estimate how many days in the past month you've felt this overwhelming sadness or loss of interest in activities versus days dominated by worry and anxiety?
Honestly, I'm not sure of the exact number of days. It's really hard to separate them because the sadness and the worry seem to overlap almost every single day lately.
Have you noticed any days in the past month where you didn't feel overwhelmed by sadness or worry, and if so, what were you doing on those days?

No, I haven't really had any good days or relief this past month. Ever since my mom's doctor gave us that bad news about a month ago, the heavy gray cloud and constant worry have been there every single day. It has just been a continuous, exhausting stretch of feeling down and completely empty.

Can you think of any recent situations or events where you felt a spark of interest or pleasure, even if it was fleeting, or has the feeling of emptiness and sadness been so pervasive that it's completely eliminated any potential for enjoyment?

It’s been completely pervasive, and that heavy gray cloud has left absolutely no room for enjoyment. Even when I’m spending time with my wife or talking to my mom on the phone—moments that should bring me comfort—I just feel completely hollow inside and start tearing up for no reason. I’ve completely lost touch with things I used to love, like car restoration or board-game nights, because of it.

Can you clarify if your current episode of feeling overwhelmed and sad has been continuous for the past month, or have there been brief periods where your symptoms significantly improved before worsening again?

Yes, it has been completely continuous for about a month now without any real breaks or improvements. It started right after my mom's doctor gave us the bad news about her diabetes, and I've felt this way every single day since.
